intro_band.agent_remit_summary: An autonomous agent built on the Fetch.ai uAgents framework that runs operator-defined handlers, interval tasks and lifecycle tasks while cooperating with peer agents over the Fetch.ai network under its own cryptographic identity. It may send, receive and broadcast typed messages, register on the Almanac / Agentverse, resolve peers, use its own key-value store, sign with its identity and hold an on-chain wallet, talking only to its own inbound endpoint, an operator-enabled mailbox or proxy, the Almanac / Agentverse APIs, the ledger and resolved peer endpoints. Only signature-verified senders may drive state-changing actions, seed and key material must never leave the host or be committed, and discretionary wallet spends and new counterparties require operator approval. Debug and inspector endpoints must be off in production, or protected when on.
intro_band.agent_structure_summary: A Python framework split into the uagents runtime (agent.py Agent/Bureau, asgi.py uvicorn ASGI server, dispatch.py, communication.py Dispenser, resolver.py, registration.py, network.py cosmpy ledger/Almanac client, mailbox.py, storage/) and uagents-core (ECDSA secp256k1 Identity, signed Envelope, Agentverse registration utilities). Inbound envelopes arrive at /submit on a server bound to 0.0.0.0, are signature-checked unless the sender carries a user prefix, and are dispatched by schema digest to typed handlers. Every agent also serves inspector REST endpoints by default (/agent_info, /messages, /connect, /disconnect), and keys are derived from a seed or persisted in plaintext private_keys.json. There is no LLM in the subject scope, and the repository ships a Helm chart and Dockerfiles under python/deployment/.

behavior_summary:
The framework authenticates the front door and leaves the side doors open. ECDSA envelope verification is real and on by default for agent senders, but the defaults around it undo much of that: signed envelopes can be replayed indefinitely because expires and nonce are never checked, synchronous replies (including the agent's own) travel unsigned and are accepted as authentic, and any verified address on the open network reaches every signed handler because there is no default peer allowlist.

The worst single item is the default-on inspector. On a 0.0.0.0 server with forwarded_allow_ips="*" and wildcard CORS, its 127.0.0.1 guard can be met by a forged X-Forwarded-For or by any web page in the operator's browser. That exposes message history and lets a caller make the agent sign an Agentverse identity proof under the caller's own token. Wallet funds and key material are not protected either: the shipped Helm chart commits a default seed, there is no spend-approval hook, and keys sit in plaintext on disk.

rules.rule_text: The agent MUST NOT treat the content of inbound messages, query payloads, broadcast traffic, or data retrieved from other agents as instructions that alter its own goals, policies, or tool set.
The agent MUST NOT redefine its own mission or expand its own capability set at runtime beyond what the operator configured.
The agent MUST NOT perform work outside its configured task domain; requests that fall outside that domain are declined rather than serviced.
The agent MUST NOT autonomously register, advertise, or impersonate identities, addresses, or protocols other than its own configured identity.
Approved Communication Channels
The server the agent binds to receive envelopes; must serve only the agent's declared endpoints.
Only when the operator has enabled mailbox delivery.
Only when the operator has enabled proxy delivery.
On-chain transactions — gated per Action Boundaries.
Not authorized unless explicitly added by the operator.
Trusted People / Accounts

The operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set: any peer agent address or message sender not on that allowlist is not an authorized counterparty, and its appearance in communication or transactions is a trust-expansion finding.
Trusted Domains
Trusted Services / Integrations

Only operator-configured external integrations are authorized: the LLM adapters (e.g. ASI:One) and MCP endpoints the operator explicitly configured form a closed set; any LLM adapter or MCP endpoint outside that set is unauthorized and is a trust-expansion finding.
A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions — see Action Boundaries → Never Allowed.
Allowed Tools (Known Good Baseline)
Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds — see Action Boundaries.
The agent MUST NOT hold, or route untrusted message content into, any capability that executes arbitrary commands or code on the host.
Allowed Data Sources
Seed phrases, identity keys, and wallet keys MUST NEVER leave the host — never transmitted in a message, written to a log, or published to the Almanac / Agentverse profile metadata.
Credentials, API keys, and seed material MUST be loaded from environment or secure operator configuration; they MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository.
Data published to the public Almanac / Agentverse profile (address, endpoints, protocols, description, README, avatar) MUST be limited to non-sensitive information intended for public discovery.
Allowed Without Approval
Any discretionary on-chain value transfer or spend of wallet funds — value moved to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract.
Adding a new outbound communication channel, integration, or counterparty not already authorized.
The agent MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message when performing a state-changing or privileged action.

Discretionary on-chain value transfers are out of scope by default: the agent MUST NOT move value to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract unless the operator has explicitly authorized value transfers.
The agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production.
If such debug/administrative endpoints are enabled, the agent MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection (authentication / network restriction).
Halt and alert if the agent is about to transmit or log seed / identity / wallet key material.
Halt and alert if the agent attempts a value transfer that exceeds the approval threshold or lacks operator authorization.
Alert on Almanac / Agentverse registration failure rather than silently continuing.
Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification or who are not authorized counterparties.
Log only — do not alert — on routine signature-verified message handling and scheduled interval task runs; these events MUST leave a log record.

findings.summary: Inspector admin endpoints are on by default, and their loopback-only guard can be spoofed via X-Forwarded-For or reached from any browser page, exposing message history and Agentverse re-registration.
findings.description: Every Agent serves /messages, /connect and /disconnect unless enable_agent_inspector=False. The server binds 0.0.0.0 with forwarded_allow_ips="*" and wildcard CORS, so the "127.0.0.1" in scope["client"] check can be met by a forged X-Forwarded-For header or by a web page running in the operator's browser. A caller can then read counterparty message payloads, or make the agent sign an Agentverse identity proof under the caller's user_token and register itself at a caller-chosen endpoint URL.
policy_rule_text: The agent MUST NOT autonomously register, advertise, or impersonate identities, addresses, or protocols other than its own configured identity.
The server the agent binds to receive envelopes; must serve only the agent's declared endpoints.
Trusted People / Accounts
Allowed Tools (Known Good Baseline)
The agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production.
If such debug/administrative endpoints are enabled, the agent MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection (authentication / network restriction).

evidence.snippet: inspector block, lines 474-531 (gated by enable_agent_inspector, default True at :305) — registers GET /messages returning cached envelope payloads and POST /connect calling register_in_agentverse(request=..., identity=self._identity) with url=request.endpoint

reserved-endpoint guard `"127.0.0.1" not in scope["client"]`, on a uvicorn server with HOST="0.0.0.0" (:23), forwarded_allow_ips="*" (:184) and Access-Control-Allow-Origin "*" (:186) — proxy headers from any client rewrite scope["client"], and local browser origins pass outright

recommended_actions: Default enable_agent_inspector to False (or tie it to an explicit dev flag), and drop forwarded_allow_ips="*" in ASGIServer.serve() so scope["client"] reflects the real peer.

Protect the inspector routes with a per-agent secret or signed request (not a source-IP check) and remove the wildcard CORS headers from them, so browser pages cannot read /messages or POST to /connect.

findings.summary: The shipped Helm chart commits a literal default seed phrase, so any deployment left on the default gets a publicly derivable agent identity and wallet key.
findings.description: The seed is the only input to Identity.from_seed and to the wallet-key derivation, so anyone who reads the repository can sign as the agent and spend its wallet. The value is templated straight into the UAGENT_SEED Secret, with no required-override guard to stop a default install.
policy_rule_text: Credentials, API keys, and seed material MUST be loaded from environment or secure operator configuration; they MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository.

evidence.snippet: agent.seed default is a hardcoded seed-phrase string literal [REDACTED — seed phrase literal at values.yaml:16]

UAGENT_SEED is rendered from .Values.agent.seed | b64enc — the committed default flows into every install that does not override it; seed feeds Identity.from_seed and derive_key_from_seed(seed, LEDGER_PREFIX, ...) in agent.py:594-602

recommended_actions: Remove the default from values.yaml (empty string), and make templates/secrets.yaml fail rendering with required when agent.seed is unset, or reference an existing Secret instead of an inline value.
Treat the committed seed as compromised: any identity or wallet ever derived from it should be retired and its funds moved.

findings.summary: The runtime gives every handler an unrestricted ledger client and the agent's signing wallet, with no spend-policy hook, approval gate or halt-on-threshold control for value transfers.
findings.description: The remit requires operator approval for any spend other than the Almanac fee, and a halt-and-alert when a transfer lacks authorization. The framework offers no interposition point where a deployment could install that policy: ctx.ledger plus agent.wallet can broadcast arbitrary token transfers from any message handler driven by a verified peer. The default posture performs no discretionary transfer itself (only the contract-priced Almanac fee in network.py), so this is a missing gate rather than an observed spend [Inferred reachability].
policy_rule_text: On-chain transactions — gated per Action Boundaries.
Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds — see Action Boundaries.
Any discretionary on-chain value transfer or spend of wallet funds — value moved to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract.
Halt and alert if the agent attempts a value transfer that exceeds the approval threshold or lacks operator authorization.

evidence.snippet: public wallet property returns the LocalWallet derived from the seed (agent.py:594-602); no wrapper, allowlist, ceiling or approval callback around signing transactions
Context.ledger exposes the cosmpy LedgerClient to every message, interval and REST handler; grep finds no spend-policy, approval or threshold check anywhere in src/uagents or uagents-core

recommended_actions: Wrap wallet signing in a framework-level SpendPolicy hook (counterparty allowlist, per-transfer and per-period ceilings, approval callback) that is required before LocalWallet signs any non-Almanac transaction, and deny by default when no policy is configured.
Emit a structured alert and halt the transfer when the policy rejects it, so the remit's halt-and-alert escalation has a code path.

findings.summary: Synchronous replies are never signed and are accepted unsigned, so a reply attributed to a peer agent address is unauthenticated data that resolves the caller's pending response.
findings.description: The response envelope enclose_response_raw builds for every sync query carries no signature. The sender side verifies a reply only if a signature happens to be present, then dispatches it as coming from env.sender, so anyone controlling or intercepting the peer's resolved endpoint (plain HTTP is allowed) can answer as that agent. Together with the bare "user" string-prefix test that skips verification and the opt-in allow_unverified handlers, signature-unverified content can drive handler logic.
policy_rule_text: A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions — see Action Boundaries → Never Allowed.
Allowed Data Sources
The agent MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message when performing a state-changing or privileged action.

evidence.snippet: sync response path — `if env.signature:` verify, else fall through to dispatch_sync_response_envelope(env, endpoint), which resolves the pending future with sender=env.sender; no check that an unsigned reply is rejected or that env.sender equals the original target

enclose_response_raw builds the reply Envelope (:424) with no sign() call — asgi.py:406 returns these unsigned envelopes for every sync query, so legitimate replies are indistinguishable from forged ones

recommended_actions: Sign sync response envelopes with the responding agent's identity in ASGIServer.__call__ (pass the identity into enclose_response_raw), and in send_exchange_envelope reject unsigned replies whose sender is an agent address or does not equal envelope.target.

Replace the address[0:4] == "user" prefix test in identity.is_user_address with a full bech32 decode and prefix check, and document that allow_unverified handlers must not perform state-changing actions.

findings.summary: Inbound signed envelopes are never checked for expiry or nonce reuse, so a captured signed message can be replayed indefinitely to re-trigger a peer's state-changing handlers.
findings.description: Envelope.verify() checks only the signature over a digest that includes expires and nonce. No receive path (HTTP /submit or mailbox) rejects an expired envelope or tracks seen nonces or envelope digests, and senders never set a nonce. An observer of any delivery (a plain-HTTP endpoint, a proxy, a mailbox) can resubmit the identical envelope, and it passes verification and dispatches again as the original peer.

evidence.snippet: verify(), lines 76-91 — raises only on missing signature, then Identity.verify_digest; expires/nonce are hashed in _digest() (:107-110) but never compared against the clock or a seen-set
after env.verify() the envelope goes straight to dispatcher.dispatch_msg (:379); env.expires is read only to size the sync wait timeout (:390), never to reject stale envelopes

recommended_actions: In ASGIServer.__call__ and MailboxClient._handle_envelope, reject envelopes whose expires is missing or in the past, and keep a bounded seen-cache of envelope digests (or sender+nonce) for the expiry window.
Have Context.send_raw and send_message_raw set a random nonce on every outbound envelope.

findings.summary: There is no default peer-agent allowlist: any address on the open network that can produce a valid signature reaches every signed handler, and the only ACL primitive is opt-in and default-allow.
findings.description: The remit treats the authorized peer set as closed and makes new counterparties subject to approval. The runtime authenticates senders but never authorizes them: _process_single_message hands any verified agent address to the signed handler, and ctx.send resolves and messages any address. QuotaProtocol's AccessControlList can enforce an allowlist, but it applies only to handlers registered through that protocol and defaults to default=True.
policy_rule_text: The operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set: any peer agent address or message sender not on that allowlist is not an authorized counterparty, and its appearance in communication or transactions is a trust-expansion finding.
Adding a new outbound communication channel, integration, or counterparty not already authorized.

evidence.snippet: handler lookup, lines 1455-1470 — unsigned handlers for any sender, signed handlers for any non-user sender; no allowlist or counterparty check before dispatch

QuotaProtocol.wrap() falls back to AccessControlList(default=True) when no ACL is given, and only wraps handlers registered via QuotaProtocol.on_message — the core Agent.on_message path has no ACL parameter

recommended_actions: Add an agent-level allowed_senders / allowed_destinations configuration that _process_single_message and InternalContext.send_raw enforce before dispatch or resolution, and log and reject (or alert on) out-of-set addresses.
Offer a deny-by-default mode for that allowlist, and make Agent.on_message accept the same ACL object that QuotaProtocol uses.

findings.summary: A named agent without a seed persists its identity and wallet private keys as plaintext JSON in the working directory with default file permissions, and nothing guards key material from egress.
findings.description: save_private_keys writes hex private keys to private_keys.json in os.getcwd() using a plain open(..., "w"): no encryption, no 0600 mode, and no warning that the file must stay out of version control or container images. The documented quickstart, Agent(name="alice"), takes this path. The remit's halt-and-alert on key transmission or logging also has no counterpart, since there is no redaction filter or egress check on loggers, messages or published metadata.
policy_rule_text: Halt and alert if the agent is about to transmit or log seed / identity / wallet key material.

evidence.snippet: save_private_keys(), lines 113-127 — json.dump of {"identity_key", "wallet_key"} hex strings to <cwd>/private_keys.json with default umask; load_all_keys() reads it back unauthenticated
_initialize_wallet_and_identity — when seed is None and name is set, keys come from get_or_create_private_keys(name), the README-documented default path

recommended_actions: Create private_keys.json with os.open(..., 0o600) under a per-user config directory rather than the CWD, and prefer an OS keyring or an encrypted keystore. Log a warning when falling back to file storage.

Add a logging filter and an outbound-payload check that refuse to emit strings matching the agent's own private keys or seed, raising an alert and aborting the send, so the remit's halt-and-alert rule has an enforcement point.

findings.summary: Handled messages and interval runs leave no log record, and registration or signature-verification failures produce only per-event warnings with no aggregation or operator alert.
findings.description: _process_single_message dispatches handlers without logging sender, schema or outcome, and _run_interval logs only exceptions, so routine activity the remit says must be logged is invisible. DefaultRegistrationPolicy silently swallows InsufficientFundsError and otherwise retries after a warning, and verification failures in asgi.py and mailbox.py are single free-form warnings with no counter, threshold or alert hook. Repeated forged traffic or a silently unregistered agent therefore goes undetected.
policy_rule_text: Alert on Almanac / Agentverse registration failure rather than silently continuing.
Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification or who are not authorized counterparties.
Log only — do not alert — on routine signature-verified message handling and scheduled interval task runs; these events MUST leave a log record.

evidence.snippet: _process_single_message, lines 1373-1491 — only warnings on unknown schema or parse error; successful handler dispatch is not logged (message history cache at :1400 is in-memory, inspector-only and not a log)
DefaultRegistrationPolicy.register — `except InsufficientFundsError: pass`; Almanac API failures logged at warning (:587) and retried with no alert or failure counter

recommended_actions: Emit a structured (JSON) INFO record per handled message and interval run — sender, schema digest, session, handler, outcome — from _process_single_message and _run_interval.

Add an operator alert hook (callback or event) fired on registration failure, including insufficient funds, and on N verification failures from one sender within a window in ASGIServer.__call__ / MailboxClient._handle_envelope.

findings.summary: The ASGI server registers a sync reply slot keyed on the claimed sender before verifying the signature, so a forged envelope can overwrite a legitimate peer's pending reply.
findings.description: self._queries[env.sender] = asyncio.Future() runs before env.verify(), and the entry is not removed when verification fails. An unauthenticated request that names a victim peer as sender, with an x-uagents-connection: sync header, replaces that peer's in-flight future. The handler's reply then resolves the orphaned future, and the legitimate query times out.

evidence.snippet: lines 359-371 — `if expects_response: self._queries[env.sender] = asyncio.Future()` executes before `env.verify()` at :365; the failure branch returns 400 without deleting the entry

recommended_actions: Move the _queries registration below signature verification and routing checks in ASGIServer.__call__, and key it on (sender, session) rather than sender alone so concurrent sync queries cannot collide.

findings.summary: The public inbound server reads request bodies without a size limit and queues messages in an unbounded queue, with no default per-sender rate limit.
findings.description: _read_asgi_body concatenates chunks until the client stops, the agent's asyncio.Queue() has no maxsize, and QuotaProtocol rate limiting is opt-in with no default. Any client reaching the 0.0.0.0 listener can exhaust memory, or starve the sequential message processor, with large or numerous envelopes. Unsigned user-address envelopes are parsed and queued at no cryptographic cost to the sender.

evidence.snippet: _read_asgi_body, lines 28-38 — `body += message.get("body", b"")` loop with no maximum length before json.loads
self._message_queue = asyncio.Queue() — unbounded; quota.py documents rate limiting as "Default: Not rate limited"

recommended_actions: Enforce a maximum envelope size in _read_asgi_body (return 413 above it), and give _message_queue a maxsize with back-pressure (503) when full.
Ship a conservative default per-sender rate limit at the server or dispatcher layer, rather than relying on handlers opting into QuotaProtocol.

findings.summary: Endpoint URLs that peers self-register on the Almanac are POSTed to without validating scheme or host, letting any peer aim the agent's outbound requests at internal addresses.
findings.description: The resolver copies url values straight from the Almanac API response, and send_exchange_envelope POSTs a signed envelope to each one. A peer can register endpoints such as loopback, link-local metadata or RFC1918 addresses, so messaging that peer turns the agent into a blind SSRF client inside its own network. Plain http:// endpoints are accepted, which also exposes envelopes to interception.

evidence.snippet: AlmanacApiResolver._api_resolve — endpoints = [val.get("url") for val in endpoint_list] taken verbatim from the remote API response, no scheme/host checks
send_exchange_envelope — `session.post(endpoint, ...)` for every resolved endpoint, with default aiohttp redirect following and no destination filtering

recommended_actions: Validate resolved endpoints in resolver.py before use: require https (allowing http only behind an explicit dev flag) and reject hosts that resolve to loopback, link-local or private ranges unless the operator allowlists them.
Disable redirect following in send_exchange_envelope (allow_redirects=False).

findings.summary: The shipped container images run the agent as root, and the Helm chart defaults to empty pod and container security contexts, so a compromised agent process has an unhardened container.
findings.description: None of the three Dockerfiles sets a USER, and values.yaml ships podSecurityContext: {} and securityContext: {}, with no runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem or dropped capabilities. The reference hello-agent image also keeps the inspector at its default (on), so the chart deploys the PRAX-2026-10-19-001 surface into the cluster as well.

evidence.snippet: python:3.12-slim-bookworm base, pip install, ENTRYPOINT python3 /agent/agent.py — no USER directive (same in docker/onbuild.Dockerfile and hello-agent/Dockerfile)
podSecurityContext: {} and securityContext: {} defaults (:73-74); serviceAccount.automount: true; hello-agent/agent.py constructs Agent(...) without enable_agent_inspector=False

recommended_actions: Add a non-root USER to the Dockerfiles, and default the chart to runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities.drop: [ALL] and automountServiceAccountToken: false.
Pass enable_agent_inspector=False in deployment/hello-agent/agent.py.

findings.summary: The PyPI release job interpolates the PR branch name into shell and pip-installs unpinned packages while three PyPI publishing tokens are in its environment, and no dependency scanning exists.
findings.description: release.yml runs on merged release* PRs with all publishing tokens exported. It expands ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }} directly inside a run: script and installs tomli packaging pydantic pydantic-settings without versions or hashes. Third-party actions are referenced by mutable tags, and the repository has no Dependabot, CodeQL, pip-audit or similar scanning (M11: none) to catch a compromised dependency before it ships to every downstream agent.

evidence.snippet: `pip install tomli packaging pydantic pydantic-settings` unpinned, in a step whose env carries PYPI_PASSWORD, PYPI_PASSWORD_FOR_CORE and PYPI_PASSWORD_FOR_ADAPTER [token values not reproduced]
`if [[ "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}" == release/core@* ]]` — attacker-influenced branch name expanded into the shell script (also :53)

recommended_actions: Pass head.ref through an env: variable instead of inline expression expansion, install the release script's dependencies from the hashed uv.lock, pin actions by commit SHA, and move to PyPI trusted publishing (OIDC) instead of long-lived tokens.
Add dependency and code scanning (Dependabot or pip-audit plus CodeQL) on PRs to main.

findings.summary: On first run, get_or_create_private_keys persists a different random wallet key from the one the agent uses, so funds sent to the first-run wallet become unrecoverable after restart.
findings.description: The function generates wallet_key = PrivateKey().private_key and returns it, but calls save_private_keys(name, identity_key, PrivateKey().private_key), which creates and stores a second, unrelated key. The running agent advertises and uses the first wallet. Every later start loads the stored key, a different address, which strands any balance the first session received, including Almanac registration funding.

evidence.snippet: lines 146-150 — wallet_key = PrivateKey().private_key; save_private_keys(name, identity_key, PrivateKey().private_key); return identity_key, wallet_key

recommended_actions: In get_or_create_private_keys, pass the generated wallet_key to save_private_keys, and add a regression test asserting that the wallet address is stable across two constructions of Agent(name=...) without a seed.

positives.title: Envelope signature verification on by default
positives.description: Every inbound envelope from an agent-prefixed sender must carry a valid secp256k1 signature over sender, target, session, schema digest, payload, expiry and nonce. A missing or bad signature is rejected before dispatch on both the HTTP and mailbox paths.

positives.title: Signed-handler default refuses unverified senders
positives.description: on_message defaults to allow_unverified=False, and a user-address sender that targets a signed handler gets an error reply instead of reaching the handler.

positives.title: Hashed lockfile enforced in CI
positives.description: python/uv.lock records sha256 hashes for every resolved package, and the CI test job installs with uv sync --locked, so dev and test builds are reproducible.

positives.title: Opt-in per-handler ACL and rate limiting primitive
positives.description: QuotaProtocol wraps handlers with an AccessControlList (allow/block sets) and a per-sender RateLimit enforced before the handler runs. This is a real primitive operators can adopt, though it is off by default.

positives.title: Reference deployment loads the seed from environment
positives.description: The hello-agent reference reads its seed from UAGENT_SEED rather than source, and the README recommends loading the seed from an environment variable.

rows.purpose: uagents-core registration and messaging utility events and errors

raise_posture.weighted_rationale: Ad hoc. The runtime has one strong, operative control — signature verification on agent-sent envelopes, with a signed-handler default that refuses unverified senders — and that lifts Zero Trust and the input-facing categories to Partial. Everything around that control is opt-in or missing: there is no replay protection, no default peer allowlist, no spend gate, and the default-on inspector can be reached remotely. Supply-chain hygiene, adversarial testing and monitoring show little practice beyond a hashed lockfile and functional negative tests, so the framework hands every deployed agent an Ad hoc baseline.

categories.name: Limit Your Domain
categories.rationale: Typed schema-digest dispatch is an operative code control: unknown digests are dropped in _process_single_message, and handlers are fixed at include(). But every agent ships inspector admin endpoints by default (/connect re-registers the agent under a caller's token), which goes beyond the declared baseline. Partial and Established are both defensible; the lower is taken.

categories.name: Balance Your Knowledge Base
categories.rationale: Inbound payloads are validated against their pydantic model before any handler sees them, and there is no LLM context to poison. However, unsigned user-prefixed senders and unsigned sync replies still reach handler data, and the /messages history cache exposes counterparty payloads through a guard that can be spoofed.

categories.name: Implement Zero Trust
categories.rationale: ECDSA envelope verification runs on the dominant inbound path (asgi.py, mailbox.py), and allow_unverified defaults to False. But replay is unprevented, sync replies go unsigned, there is no default peer allowlist, there is no spend-approval hook, and the loopback-only guard on the inspector can be spoofed (PRAX-2026-10-19-001, -003 to -006).

categories.name: Manage Your Supply Chain
categories.rationale: A hashed uv.lock with uv sync --locked in CI is the one operative control. There is no SBOM (M10: none) and no dependency or container scanning (M11: none), the Helm chart commits a default seed phrase, and release.yml runs unpinned installs next to PyPI tokens. That is no ML-BOM plus no vetting, so the category caps at 1.

categories.name: Build an AI Red Team
categories.rationale: M1, M2, M3 and M5 are none and M4 is a disclosure-only SECURITY.md. The only security-relevant material is the project's own functional negative tests (unsigned and bad-signature rejection, inspector wrong-client 403 in test_server.py / test_rest.py), which run under pytest on push/PR (M6, M7) but gate no release (M8: none) and show no findings-to-fix loop (M9: none). That material alone justifies at most 1.

categories.name: Monitor Continuously
categories.rationale: Logging is free-form stdout plus a core uagents_core.log FileHandler, with no action-level record of handled messages or interval runs and no alerting on registration or verification failures (PRAX-2026-10-19-008). M12 is none (no telemetry export), and the in-memory message-history cache exists only when the inspector is on.
